node_ids.description: Every task must be traceable to at least one real Atlas node. An empty array must fail validation.

canonical_ownership_note.description: Required (non-empty) for any T3 REPAIR/BUILD task before it may leave DESIGN_REQUIRED -- documents the explicit target ownership/migration semantics a human or authorized design pass has recorded.

product_decision_required.description: true if an unresolved human product decision blocks this task (checked by the RETIRE dispatch gate, see hygiene-gate.mjs).

hygiene_clearance.description: RETIRE tasks only. Current reachability (no live caller) is never sufficient justification to retire -- historical branches (Lane C repository-hygiene work) may hold unique value. Defaults to NOT_CHECKED, which blocks dispatch. Only NO_HISTORICAL_UNIQUE_VALUE or FULLY_HARVESTED, combined with a non-empty hygiene_evidence_ids, clears the gate -- see scripts/system-atlas/hygiene-gate.mjs.

hygiene_clearance_source.description: Provenance of hygiene_clearance -- a clean seam for Lane C repository-hygiene evidence to plug into later. Lane B must never hand-fabricate Lane C conclusions here.

hygiene_evidence_ids.description: e.g. branch-family:<id>, harvest:<id> -- references into future Lane C import records. Empty means no evidence exists yet, which fails the RETIRE dispatch gate closed regardless of hygiene_clearance's stated value.

status.description: PLANNED means the task appears in a wave plan only -- no real worker has claimed it. LEASED means a real Lease record (see lease.schema.json) exists for this task_id; wave planning alone must never set this. DESIGN_REQUIRED is mandatory for a T3 REPAIR/BUILD task lacking canonical_ownership_note, or for any mutating (REPAIR/BUILD/RETIRE) task lacking real owned_paths -- see mutation-ownership.mjs. RECOVERY_REQUIRED is set whenever an IN_PROGRESS task's lease ends WITHOUT an explicit completeWork() call -- either its lease expires, or its worker voluntarily releases it (see leases.mjs's releaseLease()/expireStaleLeases()). Neither event proves owned_paths were left in a safe state, so the task must not be silently reclaimed by another worker; it requires explicit evidence-backed triage via scripts/system-atlas/recovery.mjs (leases.mjs's recovery-status/resolve-recovery CLI commands) before it can leave RECOVERY_REQUIRED.
